title: United States pauses intelligence sharing with Ukraine
body:
On 5 March 2025, the Associated Press reported that the Trump administration had paused the sharing of intelligence with Ukraine. The step followed an earlier decision by President Donald Trump to pause military aid to Ukraine, and came after the televised Oval Office meeting between Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky the previous week.

The pause cut off information about Russian intentions and troop movements. Ukraine uses such intelligence to target Russian forces, including with US-supplied HIMARS and ATACMS systems. CIA Director John Ratcliffe linked the pause to what he called the "disastrous meeting" in the Oval Office. He described it as a "pause" and said Trump wanted to know that Zelensky was serious about peace.

National security adviser Mike Waltz said the administration had "taken a step back and are pausing and reviewing all aspects of this relationship." He said the pause could be lifted if both sides showed they were sincerely negotiating toward peace, including through confidence building measures. Officials indicated that the pause might be short.

It was unclear whether the suspension affected intelligence ties between Ukraine and other Western powers, including four of the Five Eyes countries. A United Kingdom spokesman would not confirm whether Britain was still passing US intelligence to Ukraine, saying only that the UK's position had not changed. Representative Jim Himes, the top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, called the withholding of intelligence "unforgivable." Ukrainian officials declined to comment on the intelligence relationship.
